The progress log says the round already raised this conflict with rule 3, that it is with the maintainer, and that nothing was built for it.

evidence.snippet: - `dispose` first writes a disposal mark to the cell, and `add` refuses a changeset whose cell holds one. Disposal is permanent: the port has no way to recreate a changeset, since one would need an incarnation every record and writer carries.

Once a changeset's records are in the store, everything local is cache, and [issue #348](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/348) may prune it. The live record is small enough to keep, so closing a pull request disposes nothing: a pull request can be reopened, and its records must still take a review. `dispose` removes a changeset's records for good, and only a writer's own command calls it.

Closing a pull request still disposes nothing, and `dispose` keeps its meaning: a writer's own command removes a changeset for good and marks it.

### Retirement

`GitRecordStore.retire(seen)` takes changeset names, each with the tree ID its folder had when the caller decided. In one commit it removes each folder whole, cell included, with no mark. A retired changeset is the same as one never written, so a reopened pull request records again from nothing. Retiring a disposed changeset takes its mark too, so a retirement undoes a disposal. That is wanted: a retirement leaves the tip as if the pull request never recorded, and a disposal's purpose, removing a changeset's records from the tip for good, holds once the job has retired it.

The round's first finding, that a retirement restarts a changeset against rule 3 of [the shared record decision](../decisions/2026-11-13-shared-record-behind-a-store-port.md), is with the maintainer, and this pass builds nothing for it.

explanation.whyHere: Rule 3 made disposal permanent because the record has no incarnation. A changeset that comes back cannot tell its old writers' records from its new ones. Every relayed round, offline dismissal and later batch carries only the changeset name. `GitRecordStore.retire` (git-record-store.ts:288, via `withoutFolders`) deletes the whole folder, `cell.json` included, and `judgeFolder` judges the mark-holding cell as clean. After that, the `disposed` refusal at git-record-store.ts:191 no longer fires for that name. The head decision picks a standard under which this is fine, but the active base text says it is not, and no maintainer ruling quoted in the decision covers it. The rulings cover the 30-day window, closed pull requests, the archived answer and rule 13.

properties.failureScenario:
1. A writer runs `dispose` on `pull-X` to remove its records for good. The cell now holds `{"disposed":true}`, and any later `add` on `pull-X` fails as `disposed` (git-record-store.ts:191).
2. Thirty days after the pull request closed, the scheduled job calls `folders()` and then `retire(new Map([["pull-X", oid]]))`. `judgeFolder` finds the cell readable and clean, so `withoutFolders` removes `changesets/pull-X/` whole, mark included. `removesOnly` accepts the commit and it is pushed. The head's own test, "takes a disposed changeset's mark with it, so an add starts it afresh" (retire.test.ts:593), shows a later `add` succeeding.
3. Any writer that still holds records under the old name can now land them, because the refusal is gone. Examples: a relay or offline dismissal that reaches the store "with the host's next add", or a re-run of an old Actions round's records job. Inferred: such a late writer exists. That step is not what breaks the rule; the removed mark is.
4. Those records join whatever the reopened or reused changeset writes next, and nothing tells the two lives apart, since no record carries an incarnation. One example: an old `round` record whose named records were not re-added reads as not reviewed for its revision. The gate takes the worst standing round, so it fails.

Disposal was permanent so that this could not happen. After the change, any retirement silently undoes it.

# The shared record branch retires the records of finished pull requests

Amends: [the shared record decision](2026-11-13-shared-record-behind-a-store-port.md), rule 13's keeping of the live record: the tip keeps open and recent pull requests' records, and a scheduled job retires the rest
Amends: [the git record store decision](2026-11-14-git-record-store-refuses-by-location.md), what a tip past a limit refuses: a retirement is the one call that still works there
Amends: [the git record store decision](2026-11-14-git-record-store-refuses-by-location.md#what-one-call-uses-and-what-bounds-it), its table of what one call uses: the rows a retirement adds

The maintainer ruled on 2026-11-21, in the coordinator's session, on [issue #617](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/617). The tip keeps the records of open pull requests and of pull requests merged in the last 30 days ([comment](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/617#issuecomment-7040616681)). A scheduled job that runs no pull request's code removes older ones. A warning shows when the store passes half of either limit. He agreed, on the same day and in the same session, to the plan's three further points ([comment](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/617#issuecomment-7052775102)):

- A pull request closed without merging keeps its records for 30 days from `closed_at`.
- A reader asked about records that have left the tip answers "archived" and names the commit that removed them.
- Removal by age amends rule 13.

The removal-only rule, the tree-ID check and the operation's name are the builder's, from [the plan](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/617#issuecomment-7049657837) and [its addendum](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/617#issuecomment-7049676449), which the coordinator read.

## The problem

Every round on the default branch relays about 26 records to `melian/state`, and nothing removes one. The tip may hold 65,536 entries and 256 MiB of records. At about 270 rounds a week, the entry lim [cut at 2 KiB]
